title: How We Grade Vintage: A, B and C Explained
excerpt: What Grade A really means, and why honest grading saves you money.

blocks.text: Every bale we ship is graded piece by piece in our Karachi warehouse. Grade A means excellent condition with minimal wear. Grade B means good, wearable vintage with light flaws. Grade C is budget stock for the price-sensitive market.
Honest grading is the whole business. One bad bale costs more than ten good ones.
Always ask for the stain rate, the size ratio and recent bale photos before you pay. A supplier who hesitates is telling you everything.

title: Why Vintage Wholesale Works in 2026
excerpt: Resale margins, demand trends and why bales beat new stock.

blocks.text: Vintage is no longer a niche. High-street shoppers want unique pieces with history, and resellers who buy graded bales at the right price per piece are making margins new clothing cannot touch.
A Grade A branded tee bale at $6 per piece resells at $18-25 in the US and UK. That is the business in one sentence.
